items.elements: One longish low note around 3-4 kHz that slurs down (0.27-0.5 s), then five short, evenly spaced clipped notes with a vertical stroke and a small flat tick at about 3.7 kHz (0.6-1.2 s), then a steep drop from about 9 to 5 kHz that runs straight into a long, finely pulsed buzz held at about 4.7 kHz (1.3-1.8 s).
items.phrase: Well, tick tick tick tick tick, wheeze.
items.grounds: A soft opening word for the low slurred note, five identical one-syllable clicks for the five clipped notes, and one long falling-then-held word for the swoop into the buzz; all of it came from the picture and none from anything I already knew.

items.elements: A series of paired notes that gets louder: each pair is a high stroke falling from about 7 to 4.5 kHz with a short flat tail, then a sharper note dipping to about 3 kHz. There is one partial note at the start, eight full pairs, and a final low slur that dips to 2 kHz and rises to 3.6 kHz.
items.phrase: And cheaper cheaper cheaper cheaper cheaper cheaper cheaper cheaper, oh.
items.grounds: The picture shows eight two-part units, each with a longer, stressed first part and a short second part, so I used a two-syllable word stressed on the first syllable, repeated eight times, with one small word at each end; honestly, reading it as repeated two-syllable pairs that get louder was primed by knowing the well-known 'teacher teacher' song, and I chose 'cheaper' on purpose to avoid that stock word.

items.elements: A falling note cut off at the start, then two matching arcs. Each arc is a slur rising from about 2.6 to 4.3 kHz, a tiny high blip near 6.3 kHz, and a slur falling from about 5.5 to 2.8 kHz. The song ends with a loud, harsh, broadband buzz at about 3-4 kHz with sweeps reaching up to 10 kHz, then a quick up-and-down stroke.
items.phrase: So up, hi, down; up, hi, down, crash, whip!
items.grounds: Each arc's rise, high blip and fall became 'up, hi, down' said twice, the cut-off falling note at the start became 'so', and the noisy broadband ending became 'crash' then a short 'whip'; all from the picture.

items.elements: Fourteen sharp notes in four groups: two notes that shoot up to about 8 kHz and drop back, two strokes falling from 7 to 4 kHz, two smaller, lower notes, four short loud checkmark notes around 3-5 kHz, and finally four loud strokes falling from 7 to about 3.5 kHz, the last one ending in an upturn.
items.phrase: Peek peek, fall fall, sink sink, tick tick tick tick, cheer cheer cheer cheery.
items.grounds: I used one one-syllable word per note, changing the word with each group as the notes went from rising, to falling, to low clipped checks, to loud falling strokes, and I gave the last note two syllables for its upturn; all from the picture.

items.elements: Two long, slow slurs rising from about 1.8 to 3.2 kHz (the second one longer), followed by five short, evenly spaced, sharp notes falling from about 3.5 to 1.7 kHz.
items.phrase: Why? Whyyy? Drop, drop, drop, drop, drop.
items.grounds: The two long rising slurs sounded to me like drawn-out questions, and the five quick falling notes like five clipped words that drop in pitch; the words came from the picture, though I recognized the pattern as resembling a cardinal before writing them and deliberately avoided the familiar 'cheer' mnemonic.
